audit.whatIsWrong: Chart reads [Swain, Swain, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill] on both layers. Packet levelChart is [Skill, Mordekaiser, Mordekaiser, Mordekaiser, Mordekaiser, Mordekaiser, Swain] at 53.85%. Every one of the page's own whys agrees with the packet and not with the chart: whys[0] 'neither side can commit', whys[1] 'you... out-trade him', whys[3] 'grind him down in every extended trade', whys[4] 'a clean solo kill', whys[6] 'Full-build Swain out-sustains you'. Separately the header block contradicts itself: diff is FAV but tone is the red #ff5d6c and report[14] calls it a Hard matchup at 7/10.
audit.why: Swain has no all-in and no sustain before 6, so Mordekaiser owns levels 2 through first item; the lane only turns once Demonic Ascension is backed by drain-mage items.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Skill, Levels 2 through First item Mordekaiser, 2+ items Swain. Ratings rescaled to match. Header made consistent: FAV, green tone, difficulty 5/10.

audit.why: Four spikes present and real: Lvl 1-2 standoff, Lvl 3-6 Q+W window, Lvl 6 Realm of Death (140/120/100s), Late Swain drain-mage items.

audit.whatIsWrong: The one mechanic that decides every trade is absent: Nevermove roots on the bolt's RETURN pass, not on the way out — Riot's text is 'It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits'. The page just says 'his catch tool. Dodge or sidestep it.' Also missing: Demonic Ascension has no fixed duration, it persists as long as he keeps draining champions, so 'when it is down' is the wrong mental model; and Ravenous Flock heals him and permanently grows his max health off Soul Fragments, which is why raw armour/MR stacking is the wrong answer and Morellonomicon is.
audit.why: Knowing the root comes back changes your footwork from 'dodge once' to 'step clear of the return path', which is the whole engage window. Knowing R is self-sustaining tells you never to wait it out.
audit.corrected: Nevermove: 850 range, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, roots on the return trip. Demonic Ascension: 120s, indefinite while he drains champions. Death's Hand 750 range 7-3s, ramps per bolt. Vision of Empire 5500-7500 range on 22-18s grants him a Soul Fragment on champion hit. Ravenous Flock heals and permanently raises his max health.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'His drain. Don't R into it.' with no cooldown, and the advice to 'engage on Demonic Ascension's cooldown' misreads an ability that has no set duration.
audit.why: Nevermove's 12-10s is the real engage clock; Ascension's 120s is the danger clock.
audit.corrected: Commit while Nevermove is down (12-10s) and never into an active Ascension (120s).

edits.before: Q start, but it's slow and telegraphed — Swain dodges it on reaction at full HP. Last-hit, aim isolated Qs only when he commits to a CS.
edits.after: Neither of you can commit at 1 — he has Death's Hand poke and no all-in, you have no shield or aura yet. Deny last-hits and dodge his bolts.

edits.before: W banks a cut of the damage you deal and take as shield-health. Short Q-auto trades now come out even or better because half the return damage gets absorbed.
edits.after: W banks a cut of the damage you deal and take as shield-health, so you eat his Death's Hand poke into the bank and win every short window from level 2.

edits.before: Riftmaker omnivamp turns the Realm 1v1 unloseable into most matchups. Swain's only outs are dodging Q forever or never being alone — neither survives a whole game.
edits.after: Full-build Swain out-sustains you: Demonic Ascension runs as long as he keeps draining, and Rylai's kites your melee. Bring Morellonomicon, R only a Swain caught alone.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 7/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Demonic Ascension and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 5/10. The lane is decided by whether you cash the early lead before his drain-mage items land.

edits.before: Hard matchup — difficulty 7/10, Swain carry threat 8/10.
edits.after: Favoured matchup — difficulty 5/10, Swain carry threat 8/10.

edits.before: Level 3 onward the lane bends your way — the Realm at 6 is the cliff. See the level-by-level chart for the swing points.
edits.after: Level 2 through first item is yours and the Realm at 6 is the cliff; the late game is his. See the chart for the swings.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Don’t R into it. Track it before every engage. - Swain Nevermove: A returning bolt that roots enemies it hits — his catch tool. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Swain Demonic Ascension: 120s, and it lasts as long as he keeps draining champions — never R into an active one. - Swain Nevermove: 850-range bolt on 12-10s; it roots on the RETURN pass, not on the way out.

edits.before: His drain. Don’t R into it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 120s drain, and it runs on while he keeps leeching. Engage off it.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Ravenous Flock heals him off Soul Fragments and stacks max HP — anti-heal it.

edits.before: Whiffing Q into the wave and trading with no passive stacks — un-isolated Obliterate hits soft, and without Darkness Rise you lose most even exchanges.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on the bolt's RETURN trip, not on the way out — step clear of its path as it comes back and his whole engage window disappears.

edits.before: Track Swain's Demonic Ascension: His drain. Don’t R into it. When it is down — R him — no drain.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on the bolt's return, not the way out. Ascension is 120s — never R into an active drain.

notes: Two structural fixes beyond the usual. (1) The header contradicted itself — diff FAV with a red tone and a 'Hard matchup, 7/10' rating line. Since the packet gives Mordekaiser five of seven rows at a 53.85% win rate, I kept FAV and brought tone, diffRating, breakdown.difficulty and report[14] into line at 5/10 rather than flipping the label. (2) The whole page told the reader to 'engage on Demonic Ascension's cooldown', which misunderstands an ultimate that has no fixed duration and persists while he drains — the engage clock is Nevermove's 12-10s, and Nevermove roots on the bolt's return pass, which had never been stated anywhere. The _missing entry (Ravenous Flock invalidating stacked resistances) is now on the page via dontsFull[1].d. Recurring kit bug unchanged: Obliterate's grounding flag is unsupported by Riot's description and I asserted nothing from it.
